20.h: 16 - ʿĀqil ibn al-Bukayr ibn ʿAbd Yā Layl ibn Nāshib al-Laythī *
20.t:
It is also said: ʿĀqil ibn Abī al-Bukayr ibn ʿAbd Yā Layl ibn Nāshib ibn Ghiyarah ibn Saʿd ibn Layth ibn Bakr ibn ʿAbd Manāt ibn Kinānah al-Laythī.
Muḥammad ibn Saʿd traced his lineage and said: His name was Ghāfil, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ named him ʿĀqil.
Abū al-Bukayr was an ally of Nufayl ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā, the grandfather of ʿUmar; and Abū Maʿshar and al-Wāqidī used to say: Ibn Abī al-Bukayr.
He said: And Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah, Ibn Isḥāq and Ibn al-Kalbī used to say: Ibn Bukayr (1) .
أنبأنا محمد بن عمر، حدثنا محمد بن صالح، عن يزيد بن رومان، قال:
Ghāfil, ʿĀmir, Iyās and Khālid, the sons of Abū al-Bukayr, all embraced Islam together, and they were the first to pledge allegiance in the house of al-Arqam (2) .
وأنبأنا محمد بن عمر، حدثنا عبد الجبار بن عمارة، عن عبد الله بن أبي بكر، قال:
The sons of Abū al-Bukayr set out as emigrants, all of them, men and women, until their doors were locked.
They stayed with Rifāʿah ibn ʿAbd al-Mundhir in Medina.
Then he said: And they said:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ paired ʿĀqil and Mubashshir ibn ʿAbd al-Mundhir as brothers, and both were killed together at Badr. ⟦1:185⟧
It is also said: he paired ʿĀqil with Mujadhdhar ibn Ziyād.
ʿĀqil was martyred at the Battle of Badr, aged thirty-four.
Mālik ibn Zuhayr al-Jushamī killed him (1) .
His brother:

21.h: 17 - Khālid ibn al-Bukayr ibn ʿAbd Yā Layl ibn Nāshib al-Laythī *
21.t:
Or Ibn Abī al-Bukayr.
Ibn Saʿd said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ paired him with Zayd ibn al-Dathinnah as brothers.
Khālid took part in Badr and Uḥud, and was killed at al-Rajīʿ (2) in Ṣafar in the year 4 AH, aged thirty-four.
Their brother:

22.h: 18 - Iyās ibn Abī al-Bukayr ibn ʿAbd Yā Layl al-Laythī **
22.t:
Ibn Saʿd said (3) : The Messenger of Allah ﷺ paired him with al-Ḥārith ibn Khuzamah as brothers, and he took part in Badr and all the battles.
He also took part in the conquest of Egypt.
He died in the year 34 AH. ⟦1:186⟧
Their fourth brother:

23.t:
Ibn Saʿd said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ paired him with Thābit ibn Qays ibn Shammās as brothers.
He took part in Badr and all the battles with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
I say: No four brothers other than them took part in Badr.
ʿĀmir was martyred at the Battle of al-Yamāmah (1) .

24.h: 20 - Misṭaḥ ibn Uthāthah ibn ʿAbbād ibn al-Muṭṭalib al-Muṭṭalibī **
24.t:
Ibn ʿAbd Manāf ibn Quṣayy, al-Muṭṭalibī, the emigrant, the Badrī (البدري), mentioned in the story of the slander. ⟦1:187⟧
He was poor, and Abū Bakr used to spend on him (1) .
Ibn Saʿd mentioned him and said:
He was short, with deep-set eyes and coarse fingers, and lived fifty-six years.
He said: And he died in the year 34 AH (may Allah be pleased with him).
Beware, O audacious one (2) , of looking with a hostile eye at this Badrī (البدري) over a slip that came from him, for it has been forgiven, and he is among the people of Paradise.
And beware, O Rāfiḍah (الرافضة) (3) , of hinting at slandering the Mother of the Believers after the revealed text came down declaring her innocence, for then the Fire becomes due upon you.

25.h: 21 - Abū ʿAbs ibn Jabr ibn ʿAmr al-Awsī * (خ، ت، س)
25.t:
Ibn Zayd ibn Jusham ibn Ḥārithah ibn al-Ḥārith al-Awsī. His name was: ⟦1:188⟧
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān.
A great Badrī (البدري), who has descendants in Medina and in Baghdad.
He could write Arabic, and he and Abū Burdah ibn Niyār used to break the idols of Banū Ḥārithah.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ paired him with Khunays ibn Ḥudhāfah al-Sahmī as brothers.
He took part in Badr and the other battles, and was among those who killed Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf (1) , and ʿUmar and ʿUthmān used to send him as a collector of alms (2) .
Narrating from him: ابنه زيد، وحفيده؛ أبو عبس بن محمد بن أبي عبس، وعباية بن رفاعة.
He died in Medina in the year 34 AH, ʿUthmān prayed over him, he lived seventy years, and his grave is in al-Baqīʿ.

26.h: 22 - Ibn al-Tayyihān Abū al-Haytham Mālik ibn al-Tayyihān al-Anṣārī *
26.t:
Ibn Balī ibn ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥāf ibn Quḍāʿah al-Anṣārī, an ally of Banū ʿAbd al-Ashhal. A group said this. ⟦1:189⟧
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUmārah al-Anṣārī said: He is of the Aws, from among themselves.
Then he said: He is Ibn al-Tayyihān ibn Mālik ibn ʿAmr ibn Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Jusham ibn al-Ḥārith ibn al-Khazraj ibn ʿAmr ibn Mālik ibn al-Aws.
His mother was from Banū Jusham mentioned above.
Al-Wāqidī said: Abū al-Haytham disliked the idols in the Jāhiliyyah (الجاهلية), would show his disgust at them, and professed the oneness of Allah, he and Asʿad ibn Zurārah.
And they were among the first of the Anṣār to embrace Islam in Mecca.
He is counted among the eight who met the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in Mecca, among the six, among the twelve of the First ʿAqabah, and among the seventy (1) .
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ paired him with ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn as brothers.
He took part in Badr and the other battles, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent him to Khaybar (2) as an appraiser (3) after Ibn Rawāḥah.
And from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā ibn Ḥabbān:
That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Abū al-Haytham as an appraiser, then Abū Bakr sent him, but he refused, and said:
When I used to appraise for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and then returned, he would pray for me.
And from Ṣāliḥ ibn Kaysān, who said: Abū al-Haytham died in the caliphate (الخلافة) of ʿUmar. ⟦1:190⟧
Someone else said: He died in the year 20 AH.
Al-Wāqidī said: This is more firmly established with us than the report of those who narrated that he was killed at Ṣiffīn with ʿAlī.
أخبرنا سنقر، أخبرنا عبد اللطيف، أنبأنا عبد الحق، أنبأنا أبو الحسن الحاجب، أنبأنا أبو الحسن الحمامي، أنبأنا ابن قانع، حدثنا محمد بن بشر، حدثنا محمد بن جامع العطار، حدثنا عبد الحكيم بن منصور، حدثنا عبد الملك بن عمير، عن أبي سلمة، عن أبي الهيثم بن التيهان:
That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (The one who is consulted is trusted) (1) . ⟦1:191⟧

27.h: 23 - Abū Jandal al-ʿĀṣ ibn Suhayl ibn ʿAmr al-ʿĀmirī *
27.t:
Ibn ʿAbd Shams ibn ʿAbd Wudd ibn Naṣr ibn Ḥisl ibn ʿĀmir ibn Luʾayy ibn Ghālib ibn Fihr al-ʿĀmirī, al-Qurashī.
His name was: al-ʿĀṣ.
He was among the best of the Companions (الصحابي). He embraced Islam, and his father imprisoned him and shackled him; then on the day of the Treaty of al-Ḥudaybiyah he fled, hobbling in his shackles, while his father was present before the Prophet ﷺ for the writing of the treaty.
He said: This is the first one over whom I will hold you to account, O Muḥammad.
He said: Grant him to me.
But he refused and sent him back, while he cried out and said: O Muslims! Am I to be returned to disbelief?
Then he fled again.
He has a well-known story, mentioned in (the Ṣaḥīḥ (1)) and in the books of military campaigns.
Then he got free, emigrated, and fought in jihad, ⟦1:192⟧ then moved on to the jihad in Syria, and died a martyr in the plague of ʿAmwās in Jordan in the year 18 AH.
And his brother:

28.h: 24 - ʿAbd Allāh ibn Suhayl ibn ʿAmr
28.t:
al-ʿĀmirī *
He went out with his father to Badr concealing his faith, and when the two armies met, he went over to the Muslims, fought, and was counted a Badrī (البدري) (may Allah be pleased with him).
He had campaigns and notable stands, and was martyred at the Battle of al-Yamāmah, aged thirty-eight.
It is also said: rather, he was among the first foremost, and he emigrated to Abyssinia in the first emigration (may Allah be pleased with him).
Al-Wāqidī mentioned, saying:
When Abū Bakr led the people on pilgrimage before the Farewell Pilgrimage, Suhayl ibn ʿAmr (may Allah be pleased with him) met him and said:
It has reached me, O Abū Bakr, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (The martyr intercedes for seventy of his family (1)) .
I hope that ʿAbd Allāh will begin with me. ⟦1:193⟧
This does not hold, but he said it, if he said it, when he was martyred in the year 12 AH at al-Yamāmah.
And:

29.t:
His kunyah was: Abū Yazīd (1) .
He was the orator of Quraysh, their most eloquent, and one of their nobles.
When he came forward concerning the treaty:
The Prophet ﷺ said: (Your affair has been made easy (2)) .
His Islam was delayed until the day of the Conquest, and then his Islam became excellent.
He had been captured on the day of Badr, and got free.
He stood up in Mecca and urged the people to march out, and said: O sons of Ghālib! Will you leave Muḥammad and the apostates (3) to seize your caravan? Whoever wants wealth, here is wealth, and whoever wants strength, here is strength.
He was generous, open-handed, and eloquent.
He stood up in Mecca as an orator at the death of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with something like the sermon of al-Ṣiddīq in Medina, and calmed them and exalted Islam. ⟦1:194⟧
Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkār said: Afterwards Suhayl performed much prayer, fasting and charity, and went out with his people to Syria for jihad.
It is said: he fasted and prayed at night until his colour turned sallow and changed, and he wept much when he heard the Qurʾān.
He was a commander over a squadron (1) on the day of al-Yarmūk.
Al-Madāʾinī and others said: He was martyred on the day of al-Yarmūk (2) .
Al-Shāfiʿī and al-Wāqidī said: He died in the plague of ʿAmwās.
Narrating from him: يزيد بن عميرة الزبيدي، وغيره.

30.h: 26 - al-Barāʾ ibn Mālik ibn al-Naḍr ibn Ḍamḍam al-Anṣārī *
30.t:
Ibn Zayd ibn Ḥarām ibn Jundub ibn ʿĀmir ibn Ghanm ibn ʿAdī ibn al-Najjār al-Anṣārī, al-Najjārī, al-Madanī.
The valiant, the repeated attacker, a companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the brother of the servant of the Prophet ﷺ, Anas ibn Mālik.
He took part in Uḥud and pledged allegiance under the tree. ⟦1:195⟧
It is said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb wrote to the commanders of the army:
Do not appoint al-Barāʾ over an army, for he is one of the places of destruction, and he leads them forward into it (1) .
And it has reached us that on the day of the war against Musaylimah the Liar, al-Barāʾ ordered his companions to lift him on a shield, upon the points of their spears, and throw him into the garden.
So he plunged in among them, charged at them, and fought until he opened the gate of the garden.
That day he was wounded with some eighty wounds, and for that reason Khālid ibn al-Walīd stayed with him for a month tending his wounds (2) .
It is well known that al-Barāʾ killed a hundred brave men in single combat in his wars.
معمر: عن أيوب، عن ابن سيرين، قال:
Al-Ashʿarī said, meaning during the siege of Tustar (3) , to al-Barāʾ ibn Mālik: We have been shown a tunnel that comes out in the middle of the city, so look for some men to enter it with you.
Al-Barāʾ said to Majzaʾah ibn Thawr: Find a nimble, strong man from your people, and name him to me.
He said: Why?
He said: For a need.
He said: Then I am that man. ⟦1:196⟧
He said: We have been shown a tunnel and wish to enter it.
He said: Then I am with you.
Majzaʾah entered first of all, and when he came out of the tunnel they crushed his head with a rock; then the people came out of the tunnel, and al-Barāʾ came out and fought them in the middle of the city, and was killed (may Allah be pleased with him), and Allah granted them victory (1) .
سلامة: عن عمه عقيل، عن الزهري:
عن أنس, as a raised (المرفوع) report, he said: (How many a weak man, deemed weak, wearing two worn garments, who if he swore by Allah, He would fulfil it for him; among them is al-Barāʾ ibn Mālik).
And al-Barāʾ met the polytheists when the polytheists had inflicted harm upon the Muslims.
They said to him: O Barāʾ! The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: If you swore by Allah, He would fulfil it for you, so swear by your Lord.
He said: I swear by You, my Lord, that You grant us their shoulders; and he mentioned the hadith (2) .
عبد السلام بن مطهر: حدثنا أبو سهل البصري (3) ، عن محمد بن سيرين، ⟦1:197⟧ عن أنس:
That he entered upon his brother al-Barāʾ while he was singing, and said: Are you singing?
He said: Do you fear for me that I will die on my bed, when I have killed ninety-nine of the polytheists in single combat, apart from those in whose killing I shared with the Muslims (1) ?
In one narration: O my brother! Do you sing poetry when Allah has replaced it for you with the Qurʾān?
Ḥammād ibn Salamah said: Thābit claimed, from Anas, who said:
I entered upon al-Barāʾ while he was singing and twanging his bow, and I said: Until when this?
He said: Do you think I will die on my bed? By Allah, I have killed over ninety (2) .
ابن عون: عن محمد، قال:
Al-Barāʾ fought in single combat Marzubān al-Zārah (3) , struck him with a spear, felled him, and took his spoils (4) .
He was martyred on the day of the conquest of Tustar, in the year 20 AH. ⟦1:198⟧

31.h: 27 - Nawfal ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib al-Hāshimī *
31.t:
The cousin of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, son of al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib al-Hāshimī, Abū al-Ḥārith, the brother of Abū (1) Sufyān ibn al-Ḥārith.
Nawfal was older than his uncle al-ʿAbbās.
He attended Badr with the polytheists and was captured, and his uncle al-ʿAbbās ransomed him; then he embraced Islam and emigrated in the year of the Trench.
It is also said: the Prophet ﷺ paired him and al-ʿAbbās as brothers; the two had been partners in the Jāhiliyyah (الجاهلية), on affectionate terms.
Nawfal took part in the Pledge of Riḍwān, and helped the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of Ḥunayn with three thousand spears, and held firm with him that day. I do not know of any narration or mention of him beyond what I have given.
It is said: he died in the year 20 AH.
And it is said: he died in the year 15 AH.
He was the eldest of Banū Hāshim in his time.
And his son:

32.h: 28 - al-Ḥārith ibn Nawfal ibn al-Ḥārith al-Hāshimī **
32.t:
He embraced Islam with his father, and governed Mecca for ʿUmar and ʿUthmān.
The Prophet ﷺ had appointed him over some work.
It is said that he settled in Basra and built a house there.
He died in the caliphate (الخلافة) of ʿUthmān at about seventy years of age. ⟦1:199⟧
And his son:

33.h: 29 - ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Nawfal al-Hāshimī * (ع)
33.t:
His nickname: Bubbah.
He was born during the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ.
When Yazīd died, the people of Basra agreed to make him their governor.
Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkār said: He was the son of the sister of Muʿāwiyah ibn Abī Sufyān, and her name was: Hind.
She used to dandle him and say:
O Bubbah, O Bubbah ... I will surely marry Bubbah
to a plump, full-limbed girl ... who will lead the people of the Kaʿbah (1)
The people of Basra reached agreement and made him their commander when ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Ziyād fled, and wrote to Ibn al-Zubayr pledging allegiance to him.
He said: So he confirmed him over them.
He narrated from: عمر، وعثمان، وأبي بن كعب، وعلي، والعباس، وكعب الأحبار، وطائفة؛ and he transmitted a hadith as mursal (مرسل).
He was present at al-Jābiyah with ʿUmar.
Narrating from him: ابناه؛ إسحاق، وعبد الله، وأبو التياح يزيد بن حميد، وابن ⟦1:200⟧ شهاب، وعبد الملك بن عمير، ومولاه يزيد بن أبي زياد، وأبو إسحاق السبيعي، وعمر بن عبد العزيز، وآخرون.
Ibn Saʿd said: He is reliable (ثقة), a Successor (التابعي); his mother brought him to the Prophet ﷺ when he entered upon her, and he spat in his mouth and prayed for him (1) .
He said: And he fled from Basra to Oman out of fear of al-Ḥajjāj at the time of the revolt of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ashʿath (2) , and died in Oman in the year 84 AH.
Abū ʿUbayd said: He died in the year 83 AH.
I say: He was in his eighties, his hadith is in the Six Books (الكتب الستة), and he narrated a great deal of hadith.
He also narrated from: صفوان بن أمية، وأم هانئ بنت أبي طالب، وحكيم بن حزام.
And his son:

34.h: 30 - ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Nawfal al-Hāshimī * (خ، م)
34.t:
Abū Yaḥyā (3) al-Hāshimī, the brother of Isḥāq and Muḥammad.
He narrated from: أبيه، وابن عباس، وعبد الله بن خباب بن الأرت، وعبد الله بن شداد. ⟦1:201⟧
Narrating from him: أخوه عون، والزهري، وعاصم بن عبيد الله، وعبد الحميد الخطابي.
He was among the companions of the caliph Sulaymān.
Ibn Saʿd said: Reliable (ثقة), with few hadiths; the hot wind killed him at al-Abwāʾ (1) in the year 97 AH, while he was with the caliph Sulaymān, who prayed over him.

35.h: 31 - Saʿīd ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib *
35.t:
A cousin of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He has one hadith concerning whoever meets Allah as a believer entering Paradise (2) .
Narrating from him: Salmān al-Aghar, but in its chain of transmission (الإسناد) is Ibn Lahīʿah.
Al-Ḥākim mentioned him among the Companions (الصحابي) in his (Ṣaḥīḥ), and I have not seen anyone mention him other than him.

36.h: 32 - Abū Sufyān ibn al-Ḥārith, al-Mughīrah ibn al-Ḥārith al-Hāshimī **
36.t:
He is the cousin of the Prophet ﷺ, al-Mughīrah ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib ibn Hāshim al-Hāshimī.
The brother of Nawfal and Rabīʿah. ⟦1:202⟧
He met the Prophet ﷺ on the road before he entered Mecca, as a Muslim, and the Prophet ﷺ was disturbed and turned away from him, because things had come from him in harming the Prophet ﷺ; so he humbled himself before the Prophet ﷺ until he softened toward him.
Then his Islam became excellent, and he and al-ʿAbbās stayed close to the Messenger of Allah on the day of Ḥunayn when the people fled, and he took hold of the mule's bridle and held firm with him.
His son ʿAbd al-Malik narrated from him:
That the Prophet ﷺ said: (O Banū Hāshim! Beware of charity (1)) .
He was the foster brother of the Prophet ﷺ; Ḥalīmah nursed them both.
Hishām ibn al-Kalbī and al-Zubayr named him: Mughīrah.
A group said: His name is his kunyah, and Mughīrah was in fact their brother.
It is also said: those who resembled the Prophet ﷺ were: Jaʿfar, al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, Qutham ibn al-ʿAbbās, and Abū Sufyān ibn al-Ḥārith.
Abū Sufyān was one of the poets, and Ḥassān said of him:
Convey to Abū Sufyān from me a message carried far, for the secret has come out
You satirised Muḥammad and I answered on his behalf, and with Allah is the reward for that (2)
ابن إسحاق: عن عاصم بن عمر، عمن حدثه، قال:
The people turned back on the day of ⟦1:203⟧ Ḥunayn.
Then the Prophet ﷺ came to love this Abū Sufyān, testified for him that he would enter Paradise, and said: (I hope that he will be a successor in place of Ḥamzah (1)) .
It is said: Abū Sufyān performed pilgrimage, and the barber shaved him and cut a wart on his head, so he fell ill from it and died after his arrival in Medina, and ʿUmar prayed over him.
It is said: he died four months after his brother Nawfal ibn al-Ḥārith (2) .
Abū Isḥāq al-Sabīʿī said: When Abū Sufyān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib was dying, he said:
Do not weep for me, for I have not been stained (3) by a sin since I embraced Islam (4) .
Ibn Isḥāq said: And Abū Sufyān said, lamenting the Prophet ﷺ:
I lay sleepless, and my night passed and does not end, and the night of the one afflicted by calamity is long
Weeping aided me, and yet compared with what befell the Muslims it is little
Our calamity has grown great and weighty on the evening when it was said: The Messenger has been taken
We have lost the revelation and the sending down that was among us, with which Gabriel came and went
And that is the most deserving thing over which the souls of creation flow, or nearly flow
A Prophet who dispelled doubt from us by what was revealed to him and by what he said
And guided us so that we feared no misguidance for us, while the Messenger was our guide
We have not seen his like among the living, and among the dead he has no equal ⟦1:204⟧
O Fāṭimah, if you grieve, that is excusable, and if you do not grieve, that is the path
So return to consolation, for in it is the reward of Allah and the abundant favour
And speak of your father and do not tire, for can any saying repay the merit of your father?
For the grave of your father is the master of every grave, and in it lies the master of the people, the Messenger (1)
The line of Abū Sufyān has died out.
Ibn Saʿd said this.
حماد بن سلمة: عن علي بن زيد، عن سعيد بن المسيب:
That Abū Sufyān ibn al-Ḥārith used to pray in summer at midday, when prayer is disliked, and then pray from the noon prayer until the afternoon prayer (2) .
حماد بن سلمة: عن هشام بن عروة، عن أبيه:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (Abū Sufyān ibn al-Ḥārith is the master of the youths of the people of Paradise).
Then he performed pilgrimage, the barber shaved him, and there was a wart on his head, which he cut, and he died; so they regard him as a martyr (3) .
It is said: he died in the year 20 AH in Medina.

37.t:
Companionship; he and his father held firm with him on the day of Ḥunayn.
He lived to the middle of the caliphate (خلافة) of Muʿāwiyah.
Ibn Saʿd said this. ⟦1:205⟧
